numbered_results.result: **Finite monoids: finite type, finite dimension and bounded homology coincide.** For a finite monoid M: BM has the homotopy type of a finite complex ⇔ of a finite-dimensional complex ⇔ H_k(M; Z) = 0 for all large k; then the universal group U(M) is trivial. Corollaries: a "Swan theorem" for finite monoids (U(M) ≠ 1 forces homology in infinitely many degrees; p-locally too); finite cohomological dimension forces U(M) = 1; with Theorem C of Ben-Bassat (arXiv:2610.38760v1) the homotopy types of finite monoids with bounded homology are exactly the finite simply connected complexes.
numbered_results.proved_by: The equivalences, U(M) = 1 under bounded homology, and the corollaries: Claude Fable 5.2 (effort max), 12 Nov 2026. Before it: the finite-dimensional case (BM finite-dimensional ⇒ U(M) = 1) is G.4 of the CATHOT return (GPT-6 Astra, effort Pro); the K-theoretic proof of that case through Atiyah's (7.2), (6.11), the route that §§1–2 extend from finite dimension to bounded cohomology, was first written for this problem by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort medium), 11 Nov 2026 (`pro_reviews_20261110/1_CATHOT/REVIEW_G6.md`, route (b)), with the remark that ordinary cohomology does not suffice. The medium review did not state the bounded-homology or finite-type statements.
numbered_results.bears_on: V ms. 51–52 (Hot₀, "types d'homotopie de type fini"); sharpens G.4 of the CATHOT return, the counterexample to Ben-Bassat's Conjecture 7.1

numbered_results.result: **Miller's Theorem B under a cohomological bound.** A map BG → X, G finite, X connected with finite (or residually finite, or linear) π₁ and H^q(X; Z) = 0 for q > n, is trivial on π₁; p-local form with Z_(p) coefficients.

**A Kan–Thurston theorem without small quotients, and E.17.** Every connected CW complex W has an acyclic map BG → W such that every homomorphism from G to a group of cardinality < λ factors through π₁(W). Hence a U-small ind-object of Cat_hot is W∞-invariant iff it is ind-isomorphic to an ind-object of groupoids.
numbered_results.proved_by: The reduction of E.17 to the Kan–Thurston statement (KT_μ): first found by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort medium), 10 Nov 2026 (`pro_reviews_20261110/1_CATHOT/REVIEW.md`, "A reduction for E.17"), and put into the GALOIS prompt. (KT_μ) and E.17 for small filtered index categories: first proved by GPT-6 Astra (effort Pro) in the GALOIS return, B.10–B.12 (on file 11 Nov 2026). Re-proved independently, by a different construction, by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort max), 12 Nov 2026.

numbered_results.result: **Uncountably many maps to S².** If X is connected with H¹(X; Z) = 0 and Sⁿ is a homotopy retract of X for infinitely many n with π_n(S³) ≠ 0, then [X, S²] is uncountable.
numbered_results.bears_on: D.6 of CATHOT; V ms. 43–46 (with hunch H3)

numbered_results.result: **Posets of type RP² need at least 34 arrows** (the return proved 28).

**Census of small categories.** The fewest arrows for finite categories of types S¹, S², S³ are 4, 5, 7; S¹: only the parallel pair; S²: only the monoid P₂; every smallest S³ is a monoid. Grothendieck's own S² model (XII app. ms. 10–11) has 10 arrows.
numbered_results.proved_by: Question: CATHOT prompt, Part G (ii), Claude Fable 5.2 (effort high), 10 Nov 2026. The minima 4, 5, 7: CATHOT return G.14–G.15 (GPT-6 Astra, effort Pro; monoids of order 5 and 6 cited from Sweeney's tables). First proved without that citation by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort medium), 10 Nov 2026, by its own exhaustive enumeration of all categories with at most 6 arrows and all 208,672 labelled monoids of order 6 (`pro_reviews_20261110/1_CATHOT/REVIEW.md`, rows G.14–G.15, and `checks/`); it also found that at 5 arrows exactly the six labellings of P₂ have the homology of S², from which, with G.9, the uniqueness for S² follows (it did not state the uniqueness). Re-proved by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort max), 12 Nov 2026, with integral homology; new there: S¹ only the parallel pair, the uniqueness for S² stated, every smallest S³ a monoid (7-arrow categories with several objects), the 10 arrows of Grothendieck's model.

numbered_results.result: **A reversible fundamental localizer not detected by spectra.** W_S (homotopy cofibre null for all 2-local spheres Sⁿ, n ≥ 2) satisfies W(7), contains RP^∞ → e and not RP² → e, while every reversible localizer containing RP^∞ → e has RP² in its stable closure.
numbered_results.bears_on: POLES F.14 (1); XII §5 and XVI §3: the reversibility axiom does not single out homology theories
